Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

1. Kusalaṃ [T 5.0529][M 5.0001][V 5.0001] sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

1. Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling, a wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition. (1)

Akusalaṃ [V 5.0002] sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

Dependent on an unwholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling, an unwholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition. (1)

Abyākataṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Dependent on an indeterminate phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling, an indeterminate phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition. (1) (Abbreviated.)

2. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe tīṇi…pe… avigate tīṇi. (Saṃkhittaṃ…pe… sahajātavārampi…pe… sampayuttavārampi paṭiccavārasadisaṃ.)

2. Three by way of root condition, three by way of object condition...pe... three by way of non-disappearance condition. (Abbreviated...pe... the co-nascence section...pe... the association section is also similar to the dependence section.)

3. Kusalo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo kusalassa sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

3. A wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling by way of root condition. (1)

Akusalo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo akusalassa sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

An unwholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling is a condition for an unwholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling by way of root condition. (1)

Abyākato [M 5.0002] sukhāya vedanāya [T 5.0530] sampayutto dhammo abyākatassa sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

An indeterminate phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling by way of root condition. (1)

Kusalo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo kusalassa sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

A wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling by way of object condition. (Abbreviated.)

4. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe nava. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

4. Three by way of root condition, nine by way of object condition. (Abbreviated.)

(Yathā kusalattike pañhāvāraṃ evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ.)

(As in the question section of the wholesome triad, so should this be elaborated.)

6. One by way of root condition, two by way of object condition...pe... two by way of non-disappearance condition. (Abbreviated.) (The co-nascence section...pe... the association section is also similar to the dependence section.)

7. Akusalo dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo akusalassa dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

8. By root condition, one; by object condition, two. (Abbreviated. It should be expanded as in the question section of the wholesome triad.)

A wholesome result-producing phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome result-producing phenomenon by way of object condition. A wholesome result-producing phenomenon is a condition for an unwholesome result-producing phenomenon by way of object condition. (2)

Akusalo vipākadhammadhammo akusalassa vipākadhammadhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Akusalo vipākadhammadhammo kusalassa vipākadhammadhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

An unwholesome result-producing phenomenon is a condition for an unwholesome result-producing phenomenon by way of object condition. An unwholesome result-producing phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome result-producing phenomenon by way of object condition. (2) (Abbreviated.)

By root condition, two; by object condition, four; by dominance condition, three; by contiguity condition, two… by co-nascence condition, two; by support condition, four… by non-disappearance condition, two. (Abbreviated. It should be expanded as in the question section of the wholesome triad.)

(In the section on co-nascence... up to the section on questions, it is everywhere one.)

29. Kusalaṃ [T 5.0536] savitakkasavicāraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo savitakkasavicāro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

29. A wholesome phenomenon with applied and sustained thought conditions the arising of a wholesome phenomenon with applied and sustained thought by way of root condition. (1)

Akusalaṃ savitakkasavicāraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo savitakkasavicāro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

An unwholesome phenomenon with applied and sustained thought conditions the arising of an unwholesome phenomenon with applied and sustained thought by way of root condition. (1)

Abyākataṃ [M 5.0008] savitakkasavicāraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato savitakkasavicāro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

An indeterminate phenomenon with applied and sustained thought conditions the arising of an indeterminate phenomenon with applied and sustained thought by way of root condition. (1) (In brief.)

Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe tīṇi, avigate tīṇi. (Saṃkhittaṃ. Sahajātavārampi…pe… sampayuttavārampi paṭiccavārasadisaṃ.)

In root condition, three; in object condition, three; in non-disappearance condition, three. (In brief. The co-nascence section... and the association section are similar to the conditional section.)

30. Kusalo [V 5.0010] savitakkasavicāro dhammo kusalassa savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

30. A wholesome phenomenon with applied and sustained thought is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon with applied and sustained thought by way of root condition. (1)

Akusalo savitakkasavicāro dhammo akusalassa savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

An unwholesome phenomenon with applied and sustained thought is a condition for an unwholesome phenomenon with applied and sustained thought by way of root condition. (1)

Abyākato savitakkasavicāro dhammo abyākatassa savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

An indeterminate phenomenon with applied and sustained thought is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon with applied and sustained thought by way of root condition. (1) (In brief.)

31. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe nava, avigate tīṇi. (Saṃkhittaṃ.) (Yathā kusalattike pañhāvāraṃ evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ).

31. In root condition, three; in object condition, nine; in non-disappearance condition, three. (In brief.) (The question section should be elaborated as in the wholesome triad.)

32. Kusalaṃ avitakkavicāramattaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo avitakkavicāramatto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

32. A wholesome phenomenon without applied thought and with only sustained thought conditions the arising of a wholesome phenomenon without applied thought and with only sustained thought by way of root condition. (1)

Abyākataṃ avitakkavicāramattaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato avitakkavicāramatto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

An indeterminate phenomenon without applied thought and with only sustained thought conditions the arising of an indeterminate phenomenon without applied thought and with only sustained thought by way of root condition. (1) (In brief.)

Hetuyā [T 5.0537] dve, avigate dve. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

In root condition, two; in non-disappearance condition, two. (In brief.)

(Sahajātavārepi…pe… sampayuttavārepi pañhāvārepi sabbattha vitthāro.)

(In the co-nascence section... up to and including the association section and the question section, it is in detail throughout.)

33. Kusalaṃ avitakkaavicāraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo avitakkaavicāro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

33. A wholesome phenomenon without applied thought and without sustained thought conditions the arising of a wholesome phenomenon without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of root condition... three.

Abyākataṃ avitakkaavicāraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato avitakkaavicāro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

An indeterminate phenomenon without applied thought and without sustained thought conditions the arising of an indeterminate phenomenon without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of root condition. (1)

Kusalaṃ avitakkaavicārañca abyākataṃ avitakkaavicārañca dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato avitakkaavicāro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

A wholesome phenomenon without applied thought and without sustained thought and an indeterminate phenomenon without applied thought and without sustained thought condition the arising of an indeterminate phenomenon without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of root condition. (1) (In brief.)

Hetuyā [M 5.0009] pañca, ārammaṇe dve, avigate pañca. (Saṃkhittaṃ. Sahajātavārampi…pe… pañhāvārampi vitthāretabbaṃ.)

In root condition, five; in object condition, two; in non-disappearance condition, five. (In brief. The co-nascence section... up to and including the question section should be elaborated.)

1. Depending on a not-wholesome phenomenon, a not-wholesome phenomenon arises by root condition—depending on one unwholesome aggregate, three unwholesome aggregates and consciousness-originated matter arise…pe… two aggregates…; similarly for an indeterminate aggregate. Depending on a not-wholesome phenomenon, a not-unwholesome phenomenon arises by root condition. Depending on a not-wholesome phenomenon, a not-indeterminate phenomenon arises by root condition. Depending on a not-wholesome phenomenon, not-wholesome and not-indeterminate phenomena arise by root condition. Depending on a not-wholesome phenomenon, not-wholesome and not-unwholesome phenomena arise by root condition. Five.

2. Naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo ca naakusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Pañca.

Paccayacatukkaṃ

The Tetrad of Conditions

Hetupaccayo

Root-Condition

1. Nahetuṃ [T 6.0052][M 5.0105][V 5.0125] nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nahetuṃ akusalaṃ abyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. Nahetuṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nanahetuṃ nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nahetū akusale abyākate khandhe paṭicca hetū. Nahetuṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nakusalo ca nanahetu nakusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

1. Dependent on a rootless not-wholesome state, a rootless not-wholesome state arises by root-condition. That is: dependent on one rootless unwholesome or indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise. Dependent on a rootless not-wholesome state, a with-root not-wholesome state arises by root-condition. That is: dependent on rootless unwholesome or indeterminate aggregates, the roots arise. Dependent on a rootless not-wholesome state, both a rootless not-wholesome state and a with-root not-wholesome state arise by root-condition. (3)

Nanahetuṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nanahetu nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nanahetuṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nanahetuṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nakusalo ca nanahetu nakusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

Dependent on a with-root not-wholesome state, a with-root not-wholesome state arises by root-condition. Dependent on a with-root not-wholesome state, a rootless not-wholesome state arises by root-condition. Dependent on a with-root not-wholesome state, both a rootless not-wholesome state and a with-root not-wholesome state arise by root-condition. (3)

Nahetuṃ [V 5.0126] nakusalañca nanahetuṃ nakusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ nakusalañca nanahetuṃ nakusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nanahetu nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ nakusalañca nanahetuṃ nakusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nakusalo ca nanahetu nakusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3) (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Dependent on a rootless not-wholesome state and a with-root not-wholesome state, a rootless not-wholesome state arises by root-condition. Dependent on a rootless not-wholesome state and a with-root not-wholesome state, a with-root not-wholesome state arises by root-condition. Dependent on a rootless not-wholesome state and a with-root not-wholesome state, both a rootless not-wholesome state and a with-root not-wholesome state arise by root-condition. (3) (Abbreviated.)

2. Hetuyā [T 6.0053][M 5.0106] nava…pe… avigate nava.

2. By root-condition, nine …pe… by non-disappearance-condition, nine.

Nahetuyā dve.

By not-root-condition, two.

(Sahajātavārepi…pe… sampayuttavārepi sabbattha vitthāro.)

(The detailed explanation should be applied everywhere in the conascence section …pe… and in the association section.)

Hetu-ārammaṇapaccayā

Root-Condition and Object-Condition

3. Nanahetu nakusalo dhammo nanahetussa nakusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. Nanahetu nakusalo dhammo nahetussa nakusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. Nanahetu nakusalo dhammo nahetussa nakusalassa ca nanahetussa nakusalassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

3. A with-root not-wholesome state is a condition for a with-root not-wholesome state by way of root-condition. A with-root not-wholesome state is a condition for a rootless not-wholesome state by way of root-condition. A with-root not-wholesome state is a condition for both a rootless not-wholesome state and a with-root not-wholesome state by way of root-condition. (3)

Nahetu nakusalo dhammo nahetussa nakusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

A rootless not-wholesome state is a condition for a rootless not-wholesome state by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated.)

4. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe nava…pe… avigate nava. (Pañhāvāraṃ evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ).

4. By root-condition, three; by object-condition, nine …pe… by non-disappearance-condition, nine. (The question section should be elaborated in this way.)

5. Nahetuṃ naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nahetuṃ kusalaṃ abyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… nahetuṃ naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nanahetu naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nahetū kusale abyākate khandhe paṭicca hetū. Nahetuṃ naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu naakusalo ca nanahetu naakusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

5. Dependent on a rootless not-unwholesome state, a rootless not-unwholesome state arises by root-condition. That is: dependent on one rootless wholesome or indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise …pe… two aggregates …pe… Dependent on a rootless not-unwholesome state, a with-root not-unwholesome state arises by root-condition. That is: dependent on rootless wholesome or indeterminate aggregates, the roots arise. Dependent on a rootless not-unwholesome state, both a rootless not-unwholesome state and a with-root not-unwholesome state arise by root-condition. (3)

Nanahetuṃ naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nanahetu naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nanahetuṃ [V 5.0127] naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu [T 6.0054] naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nanahetuṃ naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu naakusalo ca nanahetu naakusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

Dependent on a with-root not-unwholesome state, a with-root not-unwholesome state arises by root-condition. Dependent on a with-root not-unwholesome state, a rootless not-unwholesome state arises by root-condition. Dependent on a with-root not-unwholesome state, both a rootless not-unwholesome state and a with-root not-unwholesome state arise by root-condition. (3)

Nahetuṃ naakusalañca nanahetuṃ naakusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ naakusalañca nanahetuṃ naakusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nanahetu naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā[M 5.0107]. Nahetuṃ naakusalañca nanahetuṃ naakusalañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu naakusalo ca nanahetu naakusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3) (Saṃkhittaṃ).

Dependent on a rootless not-unwholesome state and a with-root not-unwholesome state, a rootless not-unwholesome state arises by root-condition. Dependent on a rootless not-unwholesome state and a with-root not-unwholesome state, a with-root not-unwholesome state arises by root-condition. Dependent on a rootless not-unwholesome state and a with-root not-unwholesome state, both a rootless not-unwholesome state and a with-root not-unwholesome state arise by root-condition. (3) (Abbreviated.)

Hetuyā nava…pe… avigate nava. (Sabbattha nava.)

By root-condition, nine …pe… by non-disappearance-condition, nine. (Nine in all cases.)

6. Nahetuṃ naabyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu naabyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kusalākusalaṃ nahetuṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā, tayo khandhe paṭicca eko khandho. Nahetuṃ naabyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nanahetu naabyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ naabyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu naabyākato ca nanahetu naabyākato ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

6. Dependent on a rootless not-indeterminate state, a rootless not-indeterminate state arises by root-condition. That is: dependent on one rootless wholesome or unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises. Nasaraṇaṃ naanuttaraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nasaraṇo naanuttaro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is without refuge and not unsurpassed, a phenomenon that is without refuge and not unsurpassed arises by way of root condition. (1)

Naaraṇaṃ naanuttaraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naaraṇo naanuttaro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naaraṇaṃ naanuttaraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nasaraṇo naanuttaro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naaraṇaṃ naanuttaraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nasaraṇo naanuttaro ca naaraṇo naanuttaro ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kusalaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naabyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – kusalaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naakusalo ca naabyākato ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – kusalaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo ca naakusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – kusale khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (5)

1. Conditioned by a wholesome phenomenon, a non-wholesome phenomenon arises by way of root condition—conditioned by wholesome aggregates, mind-originated material form arises. 56. A phenomenon that is with refuge is a condition for a phenomenon that is without refuge by way of object condition, by way of co-nascence condition, by way of decisive support condition, by way of post-nascence condition, and by way of kamma condition.

Saraṇo dhammo naaraṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo, sahajātapaccayena paccayo, upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

A phenomenon that is with refuge is a condition for a phenomenon that is with conflict by way of object condition, by way of co-nascence condition, and by way of decisive support condition. (Abbreviated.)

57. Nahetuyā satta, naārammaṇe satta, naadhipatiyā satta, naanantare satta…pe… noavigate cattāri.

57. Seven by way of non-root condition, seven by way of non-object condition, seven by way of non-dominance condition, seven by way of non-contiguity condition…pe… four by way of non-disappearance condition.

Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe cattāri. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Four by way of root condition, not by way of object condition. (Abbreviated.)

Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe cattāri. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Four by way of non-root condition, by way of object condition. (Abbreviated.)

(Yathā kusalattike pañhāvāraṃ evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ.)

(As with the question section of the wholesome triad, so should it be elaborated.)

Dhammānulomapaccanīye dukapaṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Paṭṭhāna of Dyads in the Conforming and Opposing Method is concluded.

Nahetuṃ [T 6.0197] anidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu naanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ.

Conditioned by a non-root, invisible-with-impact phenomenon, a non-root, not-invisible-with-impact phenomenon arises through root condition. By root condition, one... by non-disappearance condition, one.

Hetuṃ [V 5.0255] anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu naanidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Conditioned by a root, invisible-without-impact phenomenon, a non-root, not-invisible-without-impact phenomenon arises through root condition. Conditioned by a non-root, invisible-without-impact phenomenon, a non-root, not-invisible-without-impact phenomenon arises through root condition. 32. A wholesome phenomenon that is both a root and rooted serves as object condition for a phenomenon that is neither a root nor rootless and not wholesome. A wholesome phenomenon that is both a root and rooted serves as object condition for a phenomenon that is not rootless, is a root, and is not wholesome. A wholesome phenomenon that is both a root and rooted serves as object condition for a phenomenon that is neither a root nor rootless and not wholesome, and for a phenomenon that is not rootless, is a root, and is not wholesome. (3)

Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu kusalo dhammo naahetukassa ceva nana ca hetussa nakusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Sahetuko ceva na ca hetu kusalo dhammo nahetussa ceva naahetukassa ca nakusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. A wholesome phenomenon that is rooted but not a root serves as object condition for a phenomenon that is not rootless, is a root, and is not wholesome. A wholesome phenomenon that is rooted but not a root serves as object condition for a phenomenon that is neither a root nor rootless and not wholesome. A wholesome phenomenon that is rooted but not a root serves as object condition for a phenomenon that is not rootless, is a root, and is not wholesome, and for a phenomenon that is neither a root nor rootless and not wholesome. (3)

Hetu ceva sahetuko kusalo ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu kusalo [T 6.0199] ca dhammā nahetussa ceva naahetukassa nakusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Hetu ceva sahetuko kusalo ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu kusalo ca dhammā naahetukassa ceva nana ca hetussa nakusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Hetu ceva sahetuko kusalo ca sahetuko ceva na ca hetu kusalo ca dhammā nahetussa ceva naahetukassa nakusalassa ca naahetukassa ceva nana hetussa nakusalassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (3)

Wholesome phenomena that are both a root and rooted, and wholesome phenomena that are rooted but not a root, serve as object condition for a phenomenon that is neither a root nor rootless and not wholesome. Wholesome phenomena that are both a root and rooted, and wholesome phenomena that are rooted but not a root, serve as object condition for a phenomenon that is not rootless, is a root, and is not wholesome. Wholesome phenomena that are both a root and rooted, and wholesome phenomena that are rooted but not a root, serve as object condition for a phenomenon that is neither a root nor rootless and not wholesome, and for a phenomenon that is not rootless, is a root, and is not wholesome. Ārammaṇe nava.

Nine by way of object condition.

33. An unwholesome phenomenon that is both a root and rooted serves as object condition for a phenomenon that is neither a root nor rootless and not unwholesome. (By this method, nine questions should be formulated.)

34. Hetu ceva sahetuko ca abyākato dhammo nahetussa ceva naahetukassa ca naabyākatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (Nava pañhā kātabbā.) (Saṃkhittaṃ, hetuhetusampayuttadukaṃ hetusahetukadukasadisaṃ. Saṃkhittaṃ. Nava pañhā.)

34. An indeterminate phenomenon that is both a root and rooted serves as object condition for a phenomenon that is neither a root nor rootless and not indeterminate. (Nine questions should be formulated.) (In brief, the dyad of root and associated with a root is similar to the dyad of root and rooted. In brief. Nine questions.)

Three by way of root condition… three by way of non-disappearance condition.

Nahetu-naārammaṇapaccayā

Non-Root and Non-Object Conditions

Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naārammaṇe tīṇi…pe… novigate tīṇi.

One by way of non-root condition, three by way of non-object condition… three not by way of non-disappearance condition.

(Sahajātavārampi…pe… sampayuttavārampi paṭiccavārasadisaṃ.)

(The section on co-nascence… and the section on association are similar to the section on dependence.)

Hetuyā dve, adhipatiyā dve…pe… avigate tīṇi.

Two by way of root condition, two by way of dominance condition… three by way of non-disappearance condition.

Paccanīyuddhāro

Summary of the Negative

105. Saraṇo anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo nasaraṇassa naanidassanaappaṭighassa dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo, pacchājātapaccayena paccayo, kammapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.) Nahetuyā tīṇi, naārammaṇe tīṇi…pe… noavigate tīṇi.

105. A refuge, invisible and without resistance dhamma is a condition for a non-refuge, non-invisible-without-resistance dhamma by way of co-nascence condition, by way of post-nascence condition, and by way of kamma condition. (In brief.) Three by way of non-root condition, three by way of non-object condition… three not by way of non-disappearance condition.

(Yathā kusalattike pañhāvāraṃ, evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ.)

(Just as with the question section in the wholesome triad, so should this be elaborated.)

Dhammānulomapaccanīye dukatikapaṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Paṭṭhāna of Dyads and Triads in the Conformity and Opposition section is concluded.

Kusalaṃ paccuppannārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo napaccuppannārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

When a wholesome phenomenon with the present as object is the condition, a phenomenon that is neither wholesome nor has the present as its object arises by way of root condition… There are nine by way of root condition.

31. Kusalo ajjhatto dhammo naajjhattassa nakusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)… Ārammaṇe aṭṭhārasa.

31. A wholesome, internal phenomenon is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither internal nor wholesome by way of object condition. (Abbreviated.)… There are eighteen by way of object condition.

Kusalo bahiddhā dhammo nabahiddhā nakusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)… Ārammaṇe aṭṭhārasa.

A wholesome, external phenomenon is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither external nor wholesome by way of object condition. (Abbreviated.)… There are eighteen by way of object condition.

32. Kusalaṃ ajjhattārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo naajjhattārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā [T 6.0309] nava.

32. When a wholesome phenomenon with an internal object is the condition, a phenomenon that is neither wholesome nor has an internal object arises by way of root condition… There are nine by way of root condition.

Kusalaṃ bahiddhārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo nabahiddhārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

When a wholesome phenomenon with an external object is the condition, a phenomenon that is neither wholesome nor has an external object arises by way of root condition… There are nine by way of root condition.

When an indeterminate phenomenon that is invisible and with resistance is the condition, a phenomenon that is not unwholesome and not invisible and with resistance arises by way of root condition. When an indeterminate phenomenon that is invisible and with resistance is the condition, phenomena that are not wholesome and not invisible and with resistance, and phenomena that are not unwholesome and not invisible and with resistance arise by way of root condition. Kusalaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo [T 6.0310] naanidassanaappaṭigho ca naakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

35. When a wholesome phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance is the condition, a phenomenon that is not wholesome and not invisible and without resistance arises by way of root condition. When a wholesome phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance is the condition, a phenomenon that is not unwholesome and not invisible and without resistance arises by way of root condition. When a wholesome phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance is the condition, phenomena that are not wholesome and not invisible and without resistance, and phenomena that are not unwholesome and not invisible and without resistance arise by way of root condition. There are three.

Akusalaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Akusalaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Akusalaṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho ca naakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

When an unwholesome phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance is the condition, a phenomenon that is not unwholesome and not invisible and without resistance arises by way of root condition. When an unwholesome phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance is the condition, a phenomenon that is not wholesome and not invisible and without resistance arises by way of root condition. When an unwholesome phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance is the condition, phenomena that are not wholesome and not invisible and without resistance, and phenomena that are not unwholesome and not invisible and without resistance arise by way of root condition. There are three.

Abyākataṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Abyākataṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Abyākataṃ anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho ca naakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

When an indeterminate phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance is the condition, a phenomenon that is not wholesome and not invisible and without resistance arises by way of root condition. When an indeterminate phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance is the condition, a phenomenon that is not unwholesome and not invisible and without resistance arises by way of root condition. When an indeterminate phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance is the condition, phenomena that are not wholesome and not invisible and without resistance, and phenomena that are not unwholesome and not invisible and without resistance arise by way of root condition. There are three.

Kusalaṃ anidassanaappaṭighañca abyākataṃ anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

When both a wholesome phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance and an indeterminate phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance are the conditions, a phenomenon that is not wholesome and not invisible and without resistance arises by way of root condition… There are three.

Akusalaṃ anidassanaappaṭighañca abyākataṃ anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo naanidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi… hetuyā pannarasa.

When both an unwholesome phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance and an indeterminate phenomenon that is invisible and without resistance are the conditions, a phenomenon that is not wholesome and not invisible and without resistance arises by way of root condition… There are three… There are fifteen by way of root condition.

36. Sukhāya [T 6.0311][V 5.0341] vedanāya sampayuttaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nadukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto nakusalo ca naadukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto nakusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā[M 5.0300]. 36. In dependence on a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, a not-wholesome state not associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition. In dependence on a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, a not-wholesome state not associated with painful feeling arises by way of root condition. In dependence on a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, a not-wholesome state not associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition. In dependence on a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, a not-wholesome state not associated with pleasant feeling and a not-wholesome state not associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arise by way of root condition. In dependence on a wholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, a not-wholesome state not associated with painful feeling and a not-wholesome state not associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arise by way of root condition. Seven.

In dependence on a wholesome state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, a not-wholesome state not associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition… seven… fourteen by way of root.

37. Sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… satta.

37. In dependence on an unwholesome state associated with pleasant feeling, a not-wholesome state not associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition… seven.

Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nadukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… satta.

In dependence on an unwholesome state associated with painful feeling, a not-unwholesome state not associated with painful feeling arises by way of root condition… seven.

Adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naadukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… satta. (Ekavīsati pañhā.)

In dependence on an unwholesome state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, a not-unwholesome state not associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises by way of root condition… seven. (Twenty-one questions.)

38. Sukhāya [V 5.0342] vedanāya sampayutto abyākato dhammo nasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa naabyākatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

38. An indeterminate state associated with pleasant feeling is a condition for a not-indeterminate state not associated with pleasant feeling by way of object condition. (Abbreviated.)

Ārammaṇe ekavīsati. (Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaabyākatamūlaṃ adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaabyākatamūlampi kātabbaṃ.)

Twenty-one in respect of object. (The indeterminate root-triplet associated with painful feeling and the indeterminate root-triplet associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling should also be worked out.)

39. Vipākadhammadhammaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca navipākadhammadhammo nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

39. In dependence on a wholesome state that is of the nature to produce results, a not-wholesome state that is not of the nature to produce results arises by way of root condition… three by way of root.

Vipākadhammadhammaṃ [M 5.0301] akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca navipākadhammadhammo naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

In dependence on an unwholesome state that is of the nature to produce results, a not-unwholesome state that is not of the nature to produce results arises by way of root condition… three by way of root.

Nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammaṃ [T 6.0313] abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nanevavipākanavipākadhammadhammo naabyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

In dependence on an indeterminate state that is neither resultant nor of the nature to produce results, a not-indeterminate state that is not 'neither resultant nor of the nature to produce results' arises by way of root condition… three by way of root.

40. Anupādinnupādāniyaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naupādinnupādāniyo nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

In dependence on a wholesome state that is ungrasped-at and ungraspable, a not-wholesome state that is not ungrasped-at and ungraspable arises by way of root condition… three… six by way of root.

Anupādinnupādāniyaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naupādinnupādāniyo naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

In dependence on an indeterminate state that is grasped-at and graspable, a not-indeterminate state that is not grasped-at and graspable arises by way of root condition… five by way of root.

In dependence on a wholesome state that is untainted and untaintable, a not-wholesome state that is not untainted and untaintable arises by way of root condition… three… six by way of root.

In dependence on an indeterminate state that is untainted but taintable, a not-indeterminate state that is not untainted but taintable arises by way of root condition… (abbreviated). Six by way of root… and so on… six by way of non-disappearance.

Savitakkasavicāraṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nasavitakkasavicāro naakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

In dependence on an unwholesome state accompanied by initial application and sustained application, a not-unwholesome state not accompanied by initial application and sustained application arises by way of root condition… nine by way of root.

Upekkhāsahagataṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca naupekkhāsahagato nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… satta[T 6.0315]. (Vedanāttikasadisaṃ. Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Dependent on an invisible and non-impinging unwholesome phenomenon, a phenomenon that is neither visible and impinging nor wholesome arises by root condition... Dependent on an invisible and non-impinging unwholesome phenomenon, phenomena that are neither visible and impinging nor wholesome, and phenomena that are neither invisible and non-impinging nor unwholesome arise by root condition. Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nasanidassanasappaṭigho naabyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ abyākataṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nasanidassanasappaṭigho [V 5.0345] naabyākato ca naanidassanasappaṭigho naabyākato ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi…pe… avigate tīṇi.

By condition of an invisible and non-impinging indeterminate phenomenon, a phenomenon that is neither invisible and non-impinging nor indeterminate arises by root condition. By condition of an invisible and non-impinging indeterminate phenomenon, phenomena that are neither visible and impinging nor indeterminate, and phenomena that are neither invisible and non-impinging nor indeterminate arise by root condition... three by way of root... three by non-disappearance condition.

Nahetuṃ araṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nanahetu naaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ araṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nahetu naaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ araṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nahetu naaraṇo ca nanahetu naaraṇo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Hetuyā tīṇi.

Kenaci viññeyyaṃ nahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakenaci viññeyyo nanahetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

1. Nahetuṃ [M 5.0337][V 5.0381] dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ca nahetu ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

1. Dependent on a non-root phenomenon, a root phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a non-root phenomenon, a non-root phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a non-root phenomenon, both a root phenomenon and a non-root phenomenon arise by way of root condition. (3)

Nanahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nanahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nanahetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ca nahetu ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

Dependent on a non-non-root phenomenon, a root phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a non-non-root phenomenon, a non-root phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a non-non-root phenomenon, both a root phenomenon and a non-root phenomenon arise by way of root condition. (3)

Nahetuñca nanahetuñca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuñca nanahetuñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuñca nanahetuñca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ca nahetu ca dhammā uppajjanti [T 6.0367] hetupaccayā. (3) (Saṃkhittaṃ.) Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe nava…pe… avigate nava.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is non-root and non-non-root, a root phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is non-root and non-non-root, a non-root phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is non-root and non-non-root, both a root phenomenon and a non-root phenomenon arise by way of root condition. (3) (In brief.) Nine by way of root condition, nine by way of object condition… and so forth… nine by way of non-disappearance condition.

(Sahajātavārampi…pe… pañhāvārampi vitthāretabbaṃ.)

(The co-nascence section… and so forth… and the question section should be expanded.)

2. Nasahetukaṃ [V 5.0382] dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

2. Dependent on a phenomenon without roots, a phenomenon with roots arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon without roots, a phenomenon without roots arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon without roots, both a phenomenon with roots and a phenomenon without roots arise by way of root condition. Three.

Naahetukaṃ [M 5.0338] dhammaṃ paṭicca ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is not rootless, a rootless phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not rootless, a phenomenon with roots arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not rootless, both phenomena with roots and rootless phenomena arise by way of root condition. Three.

Nasahetukañca naahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasahetukañca naahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasahetukañca naahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sahetuko ca ahetuko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi. Hetuyā nava.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither with roots nor rootless, a phenomenon with roots arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither with roots nor rootless, a rootless phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither with roots nor rootless, both a phenomenon with roots and a rootless phenomenon arise by way of root condition. Three. Nine by way of root condition.

3. Nahetusampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetusampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā [T 6.0368] nava.

3. Dependent on a phenomenon not associated with roots, a phenomenon associated with roots arises by way of root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

4. Nahetuñceva naahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

4. Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither a root nor rootless, a phenomenon that is both a root and with roots arises by way of root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

5. Nahetuñceva nahetuvippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

5. Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither a root nor dissociated from roots, a phenomenon that is both a root and associated with roots arises by way of root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

6. Nahetuṃ nasahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

6. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is without roots, a phenomenon that is not a root but is with roots arises by way of root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

7-13. Cūḷantaradukādi

7–13. The Lesser Intermediate Dyads, and so forth

7. Naappaccayaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sappaccayo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

7. Dependent on a conditioned phenomenon, a conditioned phenomenon arises by way of root condition. One by way of root condition.

8. Naasaṅkhataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca saṅkhato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā [T 6.0369] ekaṃ.

8. Dependent on a conditioned phenomenon, a conditioned phenomenon arises by way of root condition. One by way of root condition.

9. Nasanidassanaṃ [V 5.0383] dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassano dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasanidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassano dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasanidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassano ca anidassano ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Hetuyā tīṇi.

9. Dependent on a non-manifest phenomenon, a manifest phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a non-manifest phenomenon, a non-manifest phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a non-manifest phenomenon, both a manifest phenomenon and a non-manifest phenomenon arise by way of root condition. Three by way of root condition.

Nasanidassano [M 5.0339] dhammo sanidassanassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

A non-manifest phenomenon is a condition for a manifest phenomenon by way of root condition… Three.

Nasanidassano dhammo anidassanassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Naanidassano dhammo anidassanassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo.

A non-manifest phenomenon is a condition for a non-manifest phenomenon by way of object condition. A manifest phenomenon is a condition for a non-manifest phenomenon by way of object condition.

10. Nasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca appaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ [T 6.0370] paṭicca sappaṭigho ca appaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

10. Dependent on a phenomenon without impact, a phenomenon with impact arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon without impact, a phenomenon without impact arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon without impact, both a phenomenon with impact and a phenomenon without impact arise by way of root condition. Three.

Naappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca appaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sappaṭigho ca appaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

Dependent on a phenomenon with impact, a phenomenon without impact arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon with impact, a phenomenon with impact arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon with impact, both a phenomenon with impact and a phenomenon without impact arise by way of root condition. Three.

Nasappaṭighañca naappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi. Hetuyā nava.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither with impact nor without impact, a phenomenon with impact arises by way of root condition… Three. Nine by way of root condition.

11. Narūpiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca rūpī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

11. Dependent on a non-corporeal phenomenon, a corporeal phenomenon arises by way of root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

12. Nalokiyaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca lokiyo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nalokiyaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca lokuttaro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nalokiyaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca lokiyo ca lokuttaro ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

12. Dependent on a supramundane phenomenon, a mundane phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a supramundane phenomenon, a supramundane phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a supramundane phenomenon, both a mundane phenomenon and a supramundane phenomenon arise by way of root condition. (3)

Nalokuttaraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca lokiyo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1)

Dependent on a mundane phenomenon, a mundane phenomenon arises by way of root condition. (1)

Nalokiyañca [V 5.0384] nalokuttarañca dhammaṃ paṭicca lokiyo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (1). Hetuyā pañca.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither mundane nor supramundane, a mundane phenomenon arises by way of root condition. (1) Five by way of root condition.

13. Nakenaci viññeyyaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kenaci viññeyyo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

13. Dependent on a phenomenon not cognizable in a certain way, a phenomenon cognizable in a certain way arises by way of root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

14-19. Āsavagocchakaṃ

14–19. The Section on Taints

14. Naāsavaṃ [T 6.0371] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naāsavaṃ [M 5.0340] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

14. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a taint, a phenomenon that is a taint arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a taint, a phenomenon that is not a taint arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a taint, both phenomena that are taints and phenomena that are not taints arise by way of root condition. Three.

Nanoāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca noāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nanoāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nanoāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavo ca noāsavo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is a taint, a phenomenon that is not a taint arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is a taint, a phenomenon that is a taint arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is a taint, both phenomena that are taints and phenomena that are not taints arise by way of root condition. Three.

Naāsavañca nanoāsavañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi. Hetuyā nava.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither a taint nor not a taint, a phenomenon that is a taint arises by way of root condition… Three. Nine by way of root condition.

15. Nasāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sāsavo ca anāsavo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

15. Dependent on a phenomenon without taints, a phenomenon with taints arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon without taints, a phenomenon without taints arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon without taints, both phenomena with taints and phenomena without taints arise by way of root condition. Three.

Naanāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Ekaṃ.

Dependent on a phenomenon with taints, a phenomenon with taints arises by way of root condition. One.

Nasāsavañca naanāsavañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Ekaṃ. (Saṃkhittaṃ.) Hetuyā pañca.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither with taints nor without taints, a phenomenon with taints arises by way of root condition. One. (Abbreviated.) Five by way of root condition.

16. Naāsavasampayuttaṃ [T 6.0372][V 5.0385] dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavasampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

16. Dependent on a phenomenon disassociated from taints, a phenomenon associated with taints arises by way of root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

17. Naāsavañceva anāsavañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavo ceva sāsavo ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

17. Depending on a phenomenon that is neither a taint nor untainted, both a taint and a tainted phenomenon arise due to a root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

18. Naāsavañceva naāsavavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavo ceva āsavasampayutto ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

18. Depending on a phenomenon that is neither a taint nor disassociated from taints, both a taint and a phenomenon associated with taints arise due to a root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

19. Āsavavippayuttaṃ nasāsavaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca āsavavippayutto sāsavo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā pañca.

19. Depending on a phenomenon that is disassociated from taints and untainted, a tainted phenomenon that is disassociated from taints arises due to a root condition… Five by way of root condition.

20-54. Saññojanādichagocchakāni

20-54. The Six Groups Beginning with the Fetters

20. Nasaññojanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca saññojano dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā…pe….

20. Depending on a phenomenon that is not a fetter, a fetter phenomenon arises due to a root condition….

Naganthaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca gantho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā…pe….

Depending on a phenomenon that is not a bond, a bond phenomenon arises due to a root condition….

Naoghaṃ [M 5.0341] dhammaṃ paṭicca ogho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā [T 6.0373] …pe….

Depending on a phenomenon that is not a flood, a flood phenomenon arises due to a root condition….

Nayogaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca yogo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā…pe….

Depending on a phenomenon that is not a yoke, a yoke phenomenon arises due to a root condition….

Nanīvaraṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nīvaraṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā…

Depending on a phenomenon that is not a hindrance, a hindrance phenomenon arises due to a root condition…

21. Naparāmāsaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca parāmāso dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā….

21. Depending on a phenomenon that is not a clinging, a clinging phenomenon arises due to a root condition….

55-68. Mahantaradukādi

55-68. The Greater Intermediate Pairs, etc.

22. Nasārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sārammaṇo ca anārammaṇo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

22. Depending on a phenomenon without an object, a phenomenon with an object arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon without an object, a phenomenon without an object arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon without an object, both a phenomenon with an object and a phenomenon without an object arise due to a root condition. Three.

Naanārammaṇaṃ [V 5.0386] dhammaṃ paṭicca anārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

Depending on a phenomenon with an object, a phenomenon without an object arises due to a root condition… Three.

Nasārammaṇañca naanārammaṇañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi. Hetuyā nava.

Depending on a phenomenon that is neither with an object nor without an object, a phenomenon with an object arises due to a root condition… Three. Nine by way of root condition.

23. Nacittaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca citto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nocitto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca citto ca nocitto ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

23. Depending on a non-mental phenomenon, a mental phenomenon arises due to a root condition. Depending on a non-mental phenomenon, a non-mental phenomenon arises due to a root condition. Depending on a non-mental phenomenon, both mental and non-mental phenomena arise due to a root condition. Three.

Nanocittaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nocitto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Ekaṃ.

Depending on a mental phenomenon, a non-mental phenomenon arises due to a root condition. One.

Nacittañca nanocittañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nocitto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā[T 6.0374]. Ekaṃ. Hetuyā pañca.

Depending on a phenomenon that is neither mental nor non-mental, a non-mental phenomenon arises due to a root condition. One. Five by way of root condition.

24. Nacetasikaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cetasiko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacetasikaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca acetasiko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacetasikaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cetasiko ca acetasiko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Hetuyā nava.

24. Depending on a phenomenon that is not a mental concomitant, a mental concomitant phenomenon arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon that is not a mental concomitant, a phenomenon that is not a mental concomitant arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon that is not a mental concomitant, both a mental concomitant phenomenon and a phenomenon that is not a mental concomitant arise due to a root condition. Nine by way of root condition.

25. Nacittasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittavippayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittasampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasampayutto ca cittavippayutto ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

25. Depending on a phenomenon disassociated from mind, a phenomenon associated with mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon disassociated from mind, a phenomenon disassociated from mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon disassociated from mind, both a phenomenon associated with mind and a phenomenon disassociated from mind arise due to a root condition. (3)

Nacittavippayuttaṃ [M 5.0342] dhammaṃ paṭicca cittavippayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittavippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasampayutto ca cittavippayutto ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. (3)

Depending on a phenomenon associated with mind, a phenomenon disassociated from mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon associated with mind, a phenomenon associated with mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon associated with mind, both a phenomenon associated with mind and a phenomenon disassociated from mind arise due to a root condition. (3)

Nacittasampayuttañca nacittavippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi. Hetuyā nava.

Depending on a phenomenon that is neither associated with mind nor disassociated from mind, a phenomenon associated with mind arises due to a root condition… Three. Nine by way of root condition.

26. Nacittasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ [T 6.0375] dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasaṃsaṭṭho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ [V 5.0387] dhammaṃ paṭicca cittavisaṃsaṭṭho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasaṃsaṭṭho ca cittavisaṃsaṭṭho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

26. Depending on a phenomenon disjoined from mind, a phenomenon conjoined with mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon disjoined from mind, a phenomenon disjoined from mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon disjoined from mind, both a phenomenon conjoined with mind and a phenomenon disjoined from mind arise due to a root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

27. Nacittasamuṭṭhānaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittasamuṭṭhānaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nocittasamuṭṭhāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittasamuṭṭhānaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhāno ca nocittasamuṭṭhāno ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

27. Depending on a phenomenon not originated by mind, a phenomenon originated by mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon not originated by mind, a phenomenon not originated by mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon not originated by mind, both phenomena originated by mind and not originated by mind arise due to a root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

28. Nacittasahabhuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasahabhū dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittasahabhuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nocittasahabhū dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittasahabhuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasahabhū ca nocittasahabhū ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

28. Depending on a phenomenon not coexistent with mind, a phenomenon coexistent with mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon not coexistent with mind, a phenomenon not coexistent with mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon not coexistent with mind, both a phenomenon coexistent with mind and a phenomenon not coexistent with mind arise due to a root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

29. Nacittānuparivattiṃ [T 6.0376] dhammaṃ paṭicca cittānuparivattī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittānuparivattiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nocittānuparivattī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nacittānuparivattiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittānuparivattī ca nocittānuparivattī ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

29. Depending on a phenomenon not conforming to mind, a phenomenon conforming to mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon not conforming to mind, a phenomenon not conforming to mind arises due to a root condition. Depending on a phenomenon not conforming to mind, both a phenomenon conforming to mind and a phenomenon not conforming to mind arise due to a root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

30. Nacittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhāno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

30. Depending on a phenomenon not originated from being conjoined with mind, a phenomenon originated from being conjoined with mind arises due to a root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

31. Nacittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānasahabhū dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

31. Depending on a phenomenon not coexistent with that which is originated from being conjoined with mind, a phenomenon coexistent with that which is originated from being conjoined with mind arises due to a root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

32. Nacittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca cittasaṃsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānānuparivattī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

32. Depending on a phenomenon not conforming to that which is originated from being conjoined with mind, a phenomenon conforming to that which is originated from being conjoined with mind arises due to a root condition… Nine by way of root condition.

33. Naajjhattikaṃ [T 6.0377][M 5.0343] dhammaṃ paṭicca ajjhattiko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

33. Depending on a non-internal phenomenon, an internal phenomenon arises due to a root condition… Three.

Nabāhiraṃ [V 5.0388] dhammaṃ paṭicca bāhiro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi.

Depending on a non-external phenomenon, an external phenomenon arises due to a root condition… Three.

Naajjhattikañca nabāhirañca dhammaṃ paṭicca ajjhattiko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi. Hetuyā nava.

Depending on a phenomenon that is neither internal nor external, an internal phenomenon arises due to a root condition… Three. Nine by way of root condition.

Nahetupaccayo

Non-root Condition

Summary of the Negative

By way of non-root condition, seven; by way of non-object condition, seven… by way of non-non-disappearance condition, four.

(Yathā kusalattike pañhāvārassa anulomampi paccanīyampi anulomapaccanīyampi paccanīyānulomampi gaṇitaṃ, evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ.)

(Just as in the wholesome triad, the positive, the negative, the positive-negative, and the negative-positive of the question section are calculated, so too should this be calculated.)

Dhammapaccanīyānulome dukapaṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad Section in the Negative-Positive of Phenomena is concluded.

1-1. Hetuduka-kusalattikaṃ

1-1. The Root Dyad and the Wholesome Triad

1. Nahetuṃ [M 5.0349][V 5.0394] nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā hetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā nahetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā hetu kusalo ca nahetu kusalo ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Hetuyā tīṇi.

1. In dependence on a non-root, not-wholesome phenomenon, a wholesome phenomenon that is a root arises by way of root condition. In dependence on a non-root, not-wholesome phenomenon, a non-root wholesome phenomenon arises by way of root condition. In dependence on a non-root, not-wholesome phenomenon, both a wholesome phenomenon that is a root and a non-root wholesome phenomenon arise by way of root condition. By way of root condition, three.

Nahetuṃ naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā hetu akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

In dependence on a non-root, not-unwholesome phenomenon, an unwholesome phenomenon that is a root arises by way of root condition… By way of root condition, three.

2. Nahetuṃ naabyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nanahetuṃ naabyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ naabyākatañca nanahetuṃ naabyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā [T 6.0386] tīṇi.

2. In dependence on a non-root, not-indeterminate phenomenon, a non-root indeterminate phenomenon arises by way of root condition. In dependence on a not-non-root, not-indeterminate phenomenon, a non-root indeterminate phenomenon arises by way of root condition. In dependence on a non-root, not-indeterminate phenomenon and a not-non-root, not-indeterminate phenomenon, a non-root indeterminate phenomenon arises by way of root condition. By way of root condition, three.

Nasahetukaṃ naabyākatañca naahetukaṃ naabyākatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca ahetuko abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

4. In dependence on a non-root-associated, not-indeterminate phenomenon, a rootless indeterminate phenomenon arises by way of root condition. In dependence on a not-rootless, not-indeterminate phenomenon, a rootless indeterminate phenomenon arises by way of root condition. In dependence on a non-root-associated, not-indeterminate phenomenon and a not-rootless, not-indeterminate phenomenon, a rootless indeterminate phenomenon arises by way of root condition… By way of root condition, three.

5. Nahetusampayuttaṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā….

5. In dependence on a phenomenon dissociated from roots and not-wholesome…

6. Nahetu ceva naahetuko ca nakusalo dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca kusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Nahetu ceva naahetuko ca nakusalo dhammo sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa kusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Nahetu ceva naahetuko ca nakusalo dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa kusalassa ca sahetukassa ceva na ca hetussa kusalassa ca dhammassa [T 6.0387] ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Tīṇi.

6. A phenomenon that is both not a root and not rootless, and is not-wholesome, is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon that is both a root and root-associated by way of object condition. A phenomenon that is both not a root and not rootless, and is not-wholesome, is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon that is root-associated and not a root by way of object condition. A phenomenon that is both not a root and not rootless, and is not-wholesome, is a condition for wholesome phenomena that are both a root and root-associated, and that are root-associated and not a root, by way of object condition. Three.

Naahetuko ceva nana ca hetu nakusalo dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca kusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

A phenomenon that is both not rootless and not not-a-root, and is not-wholesome, is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon that is both a root and root-associated by way of object condition… Three.

Nahetu ceva naahetuko nakusalo ca naahetuko ceva nanahetu nakusalo ca dhammā hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca kusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi. (Sabbattha nava pañhā.)

Phenomena that are both not a root and not rootless, and are not-wholesome, and phenomena that are both not rootless and not not-a-root, and are not-wholesome, are conditions for a wholesome phenomenon that is both a root and root-associated by way of object condition… Three. (In all, nine questions.)

7. Nahetu ceva naahetuko ca naakusalo dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca akusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ, nava pañhā).

7. A phenomenon that is both not a root and not rootless, and is not-unwholesome, is a condition for an unwholesome phenomenon that is both a root and root-associated by way of object condition (in brief, nine questions).

Nahetu ceva naahetuko ca naabyākato dhammo hetussa ceva sahetukassa ca abyākatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi. (Nava pañhā.)

A phenomenon that is both not a root and not rootless, and is not-indeterminate, is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon that is both a root and root-associated by way of object condition… Three. (Nine questions.)

Nakenaci [M 5.0353] viññeyyaṃ nakusalañca nakenaci naviññeyyaṃ nakusalañca dhammaṃ paccayā kenaci viññeyyo kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… tīṇi. (Sabbattha nava.)

By way of a phenomenon that is not knowable by anyone and not wholesome, and a phenomenon that is not 'not knowable by anyone' and not wholesome, a wholesome phenomenon knowable by someone arises by way of root condition… three. (In all, nine.)

Nakenaci viññeyyaṃ naabyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kenaci viññeyyo abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā nava.

Nakenaci viññeyyaṃ nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kenaci naviññeyyo sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. (3)

Nakenaci naviññeyyaṃ nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca… tīṇiyeva.

Nakenaci viññeyyaṃ nasanidassanasappaṭighañca nakenaci naviññeyyaṃ nasanidassanasappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca… tīṇiyeva. (Sabbattha nava.)

Dependent on a not-cognizable-by-someone and not-visible-and-impinging phenomenon, and a cognizable-by-someone and not-visible-and-impinging phenomenon… only three. (Everywhere, nine.)

Nakenaci viññeyyaṃ naanidassanasappaṭighassa purimasadisaṃ navapañhaṃ kātabbaṃ. Nakenaci viññeyyaṃ naanidassanaappaṭighamūlassa navapañhameva. Hetuyā nava, adhipatiyā nava…pe… avigate nava.

For that which is not cognizable by anyone and not invisible-and-impinging, nine questions like the preceding should be made. For the root of that which is not cognizable by anyone and not invisible-and-non-impinging, there are just nine questions. Nine by way of root condition; nine by way of dominance condition… and so on… nine by way of non-disappearance condition.

136. Naniyataṃ [T 6.0431] nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca aniyato sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

136. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not fixed, invisible, and non-impingent, a phenomenon that is not fixed, visible, and impingent arises by way of root condition… Three by way of root.

137. Nasauttaraṃ nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sauttaro sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

137. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not superior, invisible, and non-impingent, a phenomenon that is superior, visible, and impingent arises by way of root condition… Three by way of root.

138. Nasaraṇaṃ nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca araṇo sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Ekaṃ.

138. Dependent on a phenomenon that is without defilements, invisible, and non-impingent, a phenomenon that is without defilements, visible, and impingent arises by way of root condition. One.

Naaraṇaṃ [M 5.0375] nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca araṇo sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Ekaṃ.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is with defilements, invisible, and non-impingent, a phenomenon that is without defilements, visible, and impingent arises by way of root condition. One.

Nasaraṇaṃ nasanidassanasappaṭighañca naaraṇaṃ nasanidassanasappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca araṇo sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi. (Anidassanasappaṭighe tīṇiyeva.)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is without defilements, invisible, and non-impingent, and a phenomenon that is with defilements, invisible, and non-impingent, a phenomenon that is without defilements, visible, and impingent arises by way of root condition… Three by way of root. (In the case of the invisible and non-impingent, only three.)

Nasaraṇaṃ naanidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca araṇo anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is without defilements, not invisible and non-impingent, a phenomenon that is without defilements, invisible, and non-impingent arises by way of root condition. One by way of root.

Paccanīyaṃ

The Contrary

Nahetu-naārammaṇapaccayā

Non-Root and Non-Object Conditions

139. Nasaraṇaṃ nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca araṇo sanidassanasappaṭigho [T 6.0432] dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā. Ekaṃ.

139. Dependent on a phenomenon that is without defilements, invisible, and non-impingent, a phenomenon that is without defilements, visible, and impingent arises—not by way of root condition. One.

Nasaraṇaṃ [V 5.0425] nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca araṇo sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā… tīṇi. Nahetuyā ekaṃ, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā tīṇi…pe… novigate tīṇi.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is without defilements, invisible, and non-impingent, a phenomenon that is without defilements, visible, and impingent arises—not by way of object condition… three. By non-root, one; in non-object, three; by non-predominance, three… and so on… in non-disappearance, three.

Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe tīṇi… naārammaṇapaccayā hetuyā tīṇi.

By way of root condition, in non-object, three… By way of non-object condition, in root, three.

(Sahajātavārampi paccayavārampi nissayavārampi saṃsaṭṭhavārampi sampayuttavārampi vitthāretabbaṃ.)

(The section on co-nascence, the section on conditions, the section on dependence, the section on association, and the section on conjunction should be elaborated.)

7. Pañhāvāro

7. The Question Section

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

140. Nasaraṇo nasanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo araṇassa sanidassanasappaṭighassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. Naaraṇo nasanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo araṇassa sanidassanasappaṭighassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo.

140. A phenomenon that is without defilements, invisible, and non-impingent is a condition by way of root condition for a phenomenon that is without defilements, visible, and impingent. A phenomenon that is with defilements, invisible, and non-impingent is a condition by way of root condition for a phenomenon that is without defilements, visible, and impingent.

Hetuyā dve, adhipatiyā dve…pe… avigate tīṇi.

By root, two; by predominance, two… and so on… in non-disappearance, three.

(Yathā kusalattike pañhāvārassa anulomampi paccanīyampi anulomapaccanīyampi paccanīyānulomampi gaṇitaṃ, evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ.)

(Just as in the wholesome triad, the direct order, the contrary order, the direct-contrary order, and the contrary-direct order of the question section are enumerated, so too should this be enumerated.)

Dhammapaccanīyānulome dukatikapaṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dyad-Triad Paṭṭhāna in the Contrary-Direct of Phenomena is completed.

Nakusalaṃ nanevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca abyākato nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

Dependent on a state that is not wholesome and not (to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development), an indeterminate state to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development arises by way of root condition… By way of root condition, three.

23. A not-wholesome, not-internal dhamma is a condition for an internal, wholesome dhamma by way of object condition. (In brief.) Eighteen in object condition, sixteen in dominance condition, eighteen in decisive support condition, nine in pre-nascent, presence, and non-disappearance conditions.

Nakusalo nabahiddhā dhammo bahiddhā kusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.) Ārammaṇe aṭṭhārasa, adhipatiyā cha, upanissaye aṭṭhārasa, purejāte atthiyā avigate nava.

A not-wholesome, not-external dhamma is a condition for an external, wholesome dhamma by way of object condition. (In brief.) Eighteen in object condition, six in dominance condition, eighteen in decisive support condition, nine in pre-nascent, presence, and non-disappearance conditions.

Depending on a not-unwholesome dhamma that is not visible and impinging, an indeterminate dhamma that is visible and impinging arises by way of root condition. One.

27. Nasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Dve.

27. A not-wholesome dhamma associated with not-pleasant feeling is a condition for a wholesome dhamma associated with pleasant feeling to arise by way of root condition. A not-wholesome dhamma associated with not-pleasant feeling is a condition for a wholesome dhamma associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling to arise by way of root condition. Two.

Nadukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nadukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Dve.

A not-wholesome dhamma associated with not-painful feeling is a condition for a wholesome dhamma associated with pleasant feeling to arise by way of root condition. A not-wholesome dhamma associated with not-painful feeling is a condition for a wholesome dhamma associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling to arise by way of root condition. Two.

Naadukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naadukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Dve. (Cattāri gaṇitakena dve dve pañhā kātabbā.) Hetuyā cuddasa.

A not-wholesome dhamma associated with feeling that is not neither-painful-nor-pleasant is a condition for a wholesome dhamma associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling to arise by way of root condition. A not-wholesome dhamma associated with feeling that is not neither-painful-nor-pleasant is a condition for a wholesome dhamma associated with pleasant feeling to arise by way of root condition. Two. (Four should be calculated as two questions each.) Fourteen in root condition.

28. Nasukhāya [T 6.0488] vedanāya sampayuttaṃ naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto akusalo [V 5.0464] dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekavīsa.

28. A not-unwholesome dhamma associated with not-pleasant feeling is a condition for an unwholesome dhamma associated with pleasant feeling to arise by way of root condition. A not-unwholesome dhamma associated with not-pleasant feeling is a condition for an unwholesome dhamma associated with painful feeling to arise by way of root condition. Twenty-one in root condition.

29. Nasukhāya [M 5.0412] vedanāya sampayutto naabyākato dhammo sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa abyākatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… ārammaṇe cuddasa.

29. A not-indeterminate dhamma associated with not-pleasant feeling is a condition for an indeterminate dhamma associated with pleasant feeling by way of object condition... Fourteen in object condition.
