Napītisahagato [V 5.0466] naabyākato dhammo pītisahagatassa abyākatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.) Ārammaṇe aṭṭhavīsa, adhipatiyā anantare aṭṭhavīsa…pe… upanissaye aṭṭhavīsa, kamme catuvīsa, natthiyā vigate aṭṭhavīsa.

A state that is neither accompanied-by-joy nor indeterminate is a condition for an indeterminate state accompanied by joy by way of object condition. (In brief.) By way of object, twenty-eight; by way of dominance, by way of contiguity, twenty-eight;... by way of strong support, twenty-eight; by way of kamma, twenty-four; by way of absence, by way of disappearance, twenty-eight.

Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ nakusalañca naanidassanasappaṭighaṃ nakusalañca dhammaṃ paccayā anidassanaappaṭigho kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā tīṇi.

A wholesome phenomenon that is invisible and non-impinging arises dependent on a phenomenon that is not visible and impinging and not wholesome, and a phenomenon that is not invisible and impinging and not wholesome, by way of root condition. Three by way of root.

Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ naakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā anidassanaappaṭigho akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ naabyākataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… satta.

(Naanidassanasappaṭighanaabyākatamūlāni sattameva, dukamūlāni sattameva, sabbaṃ ekavīsatimeva.)

(The roots of 'not invisible-and-impinging and not indeterminate' are indeed seven; the roots of the pair are indeed seven; the total is indeed twenty-one.)

Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ nabhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā anidassanaappaṭigho bhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is not visible-and-impinging and not to be abandoned by cultivation, an invisible-and-non-impinging phenomenon to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root condition… By way of root, three.

Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ nanevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā ekavīsa.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is not visible-and-impinging and is to be abandoned by seeing or by cultivation, a visible-and-impinging phenomenon that is to be abandoned by neither seeing nor by cultivation arises by way of root condition… By way of root, twenty-one.

59. Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ [M 5.0421][V 5.0475] naparittaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho paritto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā ekavīsa.

Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ namahaggatārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā anidassanaappaṭigho mahaggatārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is not visible-and-impinging and does not have an immeasurable object, an invisible-and-non-impinging phenomenon that has an immeasurable object arises by way of root condition… By way of root, three.

61. Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ nahīnaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā anidassanaappaṭigho hīno dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

61. A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not inferior conditions an invisible and non-impingent, inferior phenomenon to arise by way of root condition… three by way of root condition.

A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not excellent conditions an invisible and non-impingent, excellent phenomenon to arise by way of root condition… three by way of root condition.

A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not path-dominant conditions an invisible and non-impingent, path-dominant phenomenon to arise by way of root condition… three by way of root condition.

64. A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not arisen is a condition, by way of object condition, for an invisible and non-impingent, arisen phenomenon… six in object condition.

65. A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not present is a condition, by way of object condition, for an invisible and non-impingent, present phenomenon… six in object condition.

22-19. Sanidassanattika-atītārammaṇattikaṃ

66. Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ naatītārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho atītārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

66. A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not with a past object conditions an invisible and non-impingent phenomenon with a past object to arise by way of root condition… three by way of root condition.

Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ naanāgatārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā anidassanaappaṭigho anāgatārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not with a future object conditions an invisible and non-impingent phenomenon with a future object to arise by way of root condition… three by way of root condition.

Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ napaccuppannārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho paccuppannārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā [T 6.0508]… hetuyā tīṇi.

A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not with a present object conditions an invisible and non-impingent phenomenon with a present object to arise by way of root condition… three by way of root condition.

22-20-21. Sanidassanattika-ajjhattattikadvayaṃ

22-20-21. The Triad of the Visible and the Two Triads of the Internal

67. Nasanidassanasappaṭigho [M 5.0423] naajjhatto dhammo anidassanaappaṭighassa ajjhattassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.) Ārammaṇe cha, adhipatiyā cha, purejāte atthiyā avigate cha.

67. A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not internal is a condition by way of object condition for an invisible and non-impingent, internal phenomenon. (In brief.) Six in object condition, six in dominance condition, six in prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions.

Nasanidassanasappaṭigho nabahiddhā dhammo anidassanaappaṭighassa bahiddhā dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (Saṃkhittaṃ.) Ārammaṇe cha, adhipatiyā cha, purejāte atthiyā avigate cha.

A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not external is a condition by way of object condition for an invisible and non-impingent, external phenomenon. (In brief.) Six in object condition, six in dominance condition, six in prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions.

68. Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ naajjhattārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

68. A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not with an internal object conditions an invisible and non-impingent phenomenon with an internal object to arise by way of root condition… three by way of root condition.

Nasanidassanasappaṭighaṃ [V 5.0478] nabahiddhārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

A phenomenon that is not visible-and-impingent and not with an external object conditions an invisible and non-impingent phenomenon with an external object to arise by way of root condition… three by way of root condition.

(The co-nascence section, the condition section, the dependence section, the association section, the conjunction section, and the question section should be elaborated.)

Dhammapaccanīyānulome tikatikapaṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Triad-Triad Conditional Relations in the Affirmative Method of the Counter-Condition of Phenomena are finished.

Dhammapaccanīyānulome dukadukapaṭṭhānaṃ

The Dyad-Dyad Conditional Relations in the Affirmative Method of the Counter-Condition of Phenomena

1-1. Hetuduka-sahetukadukaṃ

1-1. The Root Dyad and the Rooted Dyad

1. Nahetuṃ [M 5.0425][V 5.0479] nasahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ nasahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nahetuṃ nasahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca [T 6.0509] hetu sahetuko ca nahetu sahetuko ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā. Tīṇi.

1. A phenomenon that is not a root and not rooted conditions a root, rooted phenomenon to arise by way of root condition. A phenomenon that is not a root and not rooted conditions a non-root, rooted phenomenon to arise by way of root condition. A phenomenon that is not a root and not rooted conditions root, rooted phenomena and non-root, rooted phenomena to arise by way of root condition. Three.

Nanahetuṃ nasahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Ekaṃ.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is a root and is rootless, a phenomenon that is not a root and is rooted arises by way of root condition. One.

Hetuyā cattāri, ārammaṇe cattāri…pe… avigate cattāri.

Four by way of root condition, four in object condition… four in non-disappearance condition.

2. Nanahetu naahetuko dhammo nahetussa ahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo.

2. A phenomenon that is a root and is rooted is a condition by way of root condition for a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless.

Hetuyā ekaṃ, ārammaṇe cha…pe… avigate pañca. (Pañhāvāraṃ vitthāretabbaṃ.)

One by way of root condition, six in object condition… five in non-disappearance condition. (The question section should be elaborated.)

3. Nahetuṃ naahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Ekaṃ.

3. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is rooted, a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless arises by way of root condition. One.

Nanahetuṃ [M 5.0426] naahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Ekaṃ.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is a root and is rooted, a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless arises by way of root condition. One.

Nahetuṃ naahetukañca nanahetuṃ naahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Ekaṃ. Hetuyā tīṇi.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is rooted, and a phenomenon that is a root and is rooted, a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless arises by way of root condition. One. Three by way of root condition.

1-2-5. Hetuduka-hetusampayuttādidukāni

1-2-5. The Root Dyad and the Root-Associated Dyads

4. Nahetuṃ [V 5.0480] nahetusampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu hetusampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā cattāri.

4. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and not associated with a root, a phenomenon that is a root and associated with a root arises by way of root condition… Four by way of root condition.

Nahetuṃ nahetuvippayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu hetuvippayutto [T 6.0510] dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and not dissociated from a root, a phenomenon that is not a root and dissociated from a root arises by way of root condition… Three by way of root condition.

5. Nahetuṃ nahetuñceva naahetukañca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu hetu ceva sahetuko ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

5. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is rooted, a phenomenon that is a root and is rooted arises by way of root condition. One by way of root condition.

Nanahetuṃ naahetukañceva nanahetuñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sahetuko ceva na ca hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is a root and is rooted, a phenomenon that is not a root and is rooted arises by way of root condition. One by way of root condition.

6. Nahetuṃ nahetuñceva nahetuvippayuttañca dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu hetu ceva hetusampayutto ca dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

6. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and not dissociated from a root, a phenomenon that is a root and is associated with a root arises by way of root condition. One by way of root condition.

Nanahetuṃ nahetuvippayuttañceva nanahetuñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu hetusampayutto ceva na ca hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is a root and not dissociated from a root, a phenomenon that is not a root and is associated with a root arises by way of root condition. One by way of root condition.

7. Nahetuṃ nahetuṃ nasahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nahetu sahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

7. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless, a phenomenon that is not a root and is rooted arises by way of root condition. One by way of root condition.

Nahetuṃ nahetuṃ naahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu nahetu ahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā [T 6.0511] ekaṃ.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is rooted, a phenomenon that is not a root and is rootless arises by way of root condition. One by way of root condition.

1-6-12. Hetuduka-cūḷantaradukāni

1-6-12. The Root Dyad and the Minor Intermediate Dyads

8. Nahetu [V 5.0481] nasappaccayo dhammo hetussa sappaccayassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… ārammaṇe tīṇi. (Saṅkhataṃ sappaccayasadisaṃ.)

8. A phenomenon that is not a root and is unconditioned is a condition for a phenomenon that is a root and is conditioned by way of object condition… Three in object condition. (The formed is similar to the conditioned.)

9. Nahetuṃ [M 5.0427] nasanidassanaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sanidassano dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

9. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is invisible, a phenomenon that is not a root and is visible arises by way of root condition… Three by way of root condition.

Nahetu naanidassano dhammo hetussa anidassanassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… ārammaṇe tīṇi.

A phenomenon that is not a root and is visible is a condition for a phenomenon that is a root and is invisible by way of object condition… Three in object condition.

10. Nahetuṃ nasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu sappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

10. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is without impact, a phenomenon that is not a root and is with impact arises by way of root condition… Three by way of root condition.

Nahetuṃ [T 6.0512] naappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu appaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is with impact, a phenomenon that is not a root and is without impact arises by way of root condition. One by way of root condition.

11. Nahetuṃ narūpiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu rūpī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

11. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is immaterial, a phenomenon that is a root and is material arises by way of root condition… Three by way of root condition.

Nahetuṃ naarūpiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu arūpī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is material, a phenomenon that is a root and is immaterial arises by way of root condition… Three by way of root condition.

12. Nahetuṃ nalokiyaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu lokiyo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Nanahetuṃ nalokiyaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nahetu lokiyo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā (gaṇitakena tīṇi.)

12. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a root and is supramundane, a phenomenon that is not a root and is worldly arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is a root and is supramundane, a phenomenon that is not a root and is worldly arises by way of root condition. (By calculation, three.)

Nahetuṃ nalokuttaraṃ dhammaṃ paccayā hetu lokuttaro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā… hetuyā tīṇi.

85. Nasaraṇaṃ nacittasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca araṇo cittasaṃsaṭṭho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Naaraṇaṃ nacittasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca saraṇo cittasaṃsaṭṭho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā dve.

85. Dependent on a non-refuge, non-mind-conjoined phenomenon, a non-refuge, mind-conjoined phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a refuge, non-mind-conjoined phenomenon, a refuge, mind-conjoined phenomenon arises by way of root condition. There are two by way of root.

100-83. Saraṇaduka-piṭṭhidukaṃ

100-83. The Dyad of Refuge and the Supplementary Dyad

86. Nasaraṇaṃ nadassanena pahātabbaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca saraṇo dassanena pahātabbo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

86. Dependent on a phenomenon that is a non-refuge and not to be abandoned by seeing, a phenomenon that is a refuge and is to be abandoned by seeing arises by way of root condition. One by way of root.

Naaraṇaṃ nanadassanena pahātabbaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca araṇo nadassanena pahātabbo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā [T 6.0536] ekaṃ. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

Dependent on a phenomenon that is a refuge and to be abandoned by seeing, a phenomenon that is a non-refuge and not to be abandoned by seeing arises by way of root condition. One by way of root. (Abbreviated.)

87. Nasaraṇaṃ [V 5.0496] nasauttaraṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca araṇo sauttaro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

87. Dependent on a phenomenon that is a non-refuge and not supreme, a phenomenon that is a non-refuge and supreme arises by way of root condition. One by way of root.

(Sahajātavārampi paccayavārampi nissayavārampi saṃsaṭṭhavārampi sampayuttavārampi paṭiccavārasadisaṃ.)

The sections on co-nascence, condition, support, association, and conjunction are similar to the section on dependence.

Pañhāvāro

Question Chapter

Hetu-ārammaṇapaccayā

Root and Object Conditions

88. Nasaraṇo nasauttaro dhammo araṇassa sauttarassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo. Ekaṃ.

88. A phenomenon that is not a refuge and not supreme is a condition by way of root condition for a phenomenon that is not a refuge and is supreme. One.

Nasaraṇo nasauttaro dhammo araṇassa sauttarassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ekaṃ. Hetuyā ekaṃ.

A phenomenon that is not a refuge and not supreme is a condition by way of object condition for a phenomenon that is not a refuge and is supreme. One. One by way of root condition.

Paccanīyuddhāro

Summary of the Negative

89. Nasaraṇo [M 5.0441] nasauttaro dhammo araṇassa sauttarassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… (saṃkhittaṃ.) Nahetuyā [T 6.0537] ekaṃ, naārammaṇe ekaṃ.

89. A phenomenon that is not a refuge and not supreme is a condition by way of object condition for a phenomenon that is not a refuge and is supreme... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of dependence condition... by way of post-nascence condition... (Abbreviated.) One by way of no-root condition, one by way of no-object condition.

Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe ekaṃ. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

By way of root condition, one in no-object condition. (Abbreviated.)

Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe ekaṃ. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

By way of no-root condition, one in object condition. (Abbreviated.)

(Yathā kusalattike pañhāvāraṃ evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ.)

As with the question section of the wholesome triad, so should this be elaborated.

Anuttarapadaṃ

The Unsurpassed Term

Hetu-anantarapaccayā

Root and Contiguity Conditions

90. Nasaraṇaṃ naanuttaraṃ dhammaṃ paccayā araṇo anuttaro dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā. Hetuyā ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ.

90. Dependent on a phenomenon that is not a refuge and not unsurpassed, a phenomenon that is not a refuge and is unsurpassed arises by way of root condition. One by way of root condition... one by way of non-disappearance condition.

91. Nasaraṇo [V 5.0497] naanuttaro dhammo araṇassa anuttarassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Anantare ekaṃ, samanantare ekaṃ, upanissaye dve, purejāte ekaṃ, āsevane ekaṃ, vippayutte ekaṃ, atthiyā ekaṃ, natthiyā ekaṃ, vigate ekaṃ, avigate ekaṃ.

91. A phenomenon that is not a refuge and not unsurpassed is a condition by way of contiguity condition for a phenomenon that is not a refuge and is unsurpassed. One by way of contiguity condition, one by way of immediate contiguity condition, two by way of dependence condition, one by way of pre-nascence condition, one by way of repetition condition, one by way of dissociation condition, one by way of presence condition, one by way of absence condition, one by way of disappearance condition, one by way of non-disappearance condition.

Paccanīyuddhāro

Summary of the Negative

92. Nasaraṇo naanuttaro dhammo araṇassa anuttarassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo.

92. A phenomenon that is not a refuge and not unsurpassed is a condition by way of dependence condition for a phenomenon that is not a refuge and is unsurpassed... by way of pre-nascence condition.

Naaraṇo naanuttaro dhammo araṇassa anuttarassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Nahetuyā dve, naārammaṇe dve…pe… naupanissaye ekaṃ, napurejāte dve…pe… noavigate dve.

A phenomenon that is a refuge and not unsurpassed is a condition by way of dependence condition for a phenomenon that is not a refuge and is unsurpassed. Two by way of no-root condition, two by way of no-object condition... one by way of no-dependence condition, two by way of no-pre-nascence condition... two by way of no-non-disappearance condition.

Upanissayapaccayā nahetuyā dve. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

By way of dependence condition, two by way of no-root condition. (Abbreviated.)

Nahetupaccayā [T 6.0538][M 5.0442] upanissaye dve, purejāte ekaṃ…pe… atthiyā ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ. (Saṃkhittaṃ.)

By way of no-root condition, two by way of dependence condition, one by way of pre-nascence condition... one by way of presence condition... one by way of non-disappearance condition. (Abbreviated.)

(Yathā kusalattike pañhāvāraṃ evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ.)

As with the question section of the wholesome triad, so should this be elaborated.

Anulomadukatikapaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya yāva pariyosānā tiṃsamattehi bhāṇavārehi paṭṭhānaṃ.

From the Anuloma-Duka-Tika Paṭṭhāna up to the conclusion, the Paṭṭhāna consists of approximately thirty recitation sections.

Dhammapaccanīyānulome dukadukapaṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Dukaduka Paṭṭhāna of the Dhammapaccanīyānuloma is concluded.

Paccanīyānulomapaṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Paccanīyānuloma Paṭṭhāna is concluded.

Paṭṭhānapakaraṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Book of Conditional Relations is concluded.
